title: Installing a Heat Pump Water Heater | This Old House
summary: This Old House guides viewers through replacing an aging electric water heater with a modern heat-pump model. The video contrasts a traditional glass-lined tank with two 4,500-watt immersion elements to a heat-pump system that extracts heat from surrounding air with a 700-watt compressor and circulating refrigerant. It covers why the old unit loses efficiency due to mineral buildup and demonstrates the installation workflow: shutting off water and power, draining and removing the old heater, positioning the new unit, connecting cold and hot water lines (including a vacuum breaker and dip tube), routing condensate to a pump, wiring a 240V circuit, and choosing the hybrid mode for maximum energy savings. The host emphasizes safety steps, the need for a condensate drain, and the expected energy savings from the heat-pump approach, finishing with startup and normal operation settings.

sections.title: Old water heater and observed issues
sections.description: Introduces the existing electric water heater, noting its age (about 17 years), the lack of venting, the 220V supply, and the two immersion elements (top and bottom) rated around 4,500 watts, with a warning about calcium/hardness buildup reducing efficiency and potentially causing element failure.

sections.title: Overview of the heat-pump replacement and efficiency claims
concepts: energy efficiency advantage vs traditional electric heater
sections.description: Presents the new heat-pump water heater, where the heat pump principally heats water while the traditional elements act as backups. It explains that the heat pump uses the refrigerant cycle to move heat from ambient air into the tank and highlights the efficiency advantage (compressor ~700 W versus 4,500 W electric elements) and the expected energy savings.

sections.title: Removal of old unit and placement of the new heater
sections.description: Covers the process of preparing for replacement: turning off the water, cutting power, draining and removing the old unit, and bringing the new heat-pump unit into position while aligning it with the plumbing.

sections.title: Water connections: vacuum breaker, dip tube, and pipe unions
sections.description: Details the water connections for the new heater, including the cold-water feed with a dip tube to deliver cold water to the tank bottom, the hot-water outlet back to the house, a vacuum breaker to prevent air-induced damage, and the unions used for serviceability.

sections.title: Electrical hookup, condensate management, and startup settings
concepts: two hot legs and a ground
sections.description: Covers wiring the 240V supply (two hot legs and ground), addressing condensate produced by the heat pump via a condensate pump routed to a drain, installing a filter, and configuring the unit to the default 120°F with the hybrid mode to maximize efficiency during operation and startup.
